item.title: Incarico post-doc: Development of quantitative tools for insect population dynamics (Univ. BRESCIA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-26 14:00
Institution: Univ. BRESCIA, Brescia
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-05 Patologia vegetale ed entomologia

The research activity will focus on developing innovative approaches for modelling and predicting the dynamics of insect populations of agricultural relevance. It will include the development of mathematical and statistical models, estimation of biological parameters and functional relationships, model calibration and uncertainty quantification, integrating data from laboratory experiments, field monitoring and scientific literature. Statistical and machine-learning approaches will be explored to improve model inference and predictive performance. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Molecular anatomy of stem cell niches during aging (Univ. PARMA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-20 23:59
Institution: Univ. PARMA, Parma
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/MVET-01 Anatomia e fisiologia veterinaria

This project aims to characterize the anatomical and molecular changes occurring in stem cell niches by integrating advanced spatial profiling technologies with histological and molecular analyses, in order to identify the anatomical and molecular determinants underlying the age-related decline in regenerative function. The objective is to define how the structural and functional organization of stem cell niches is remodeled during aging and to identify spatial molecular signatures associated with pro-regenerative or pro-senescent states. item.title: Incarico post-doc: Fecal and Serum Biomarkers in Gastrointestinal Diseases of Dogs and Cats: From Diagnosis to Disease Monitoring and Characterization (Univ. PARMA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 23:59
Institution: Univ. PARMA, Parma
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/MVET-04 Clinica medica farmacologia e tossicologia veterinaria

This project aims to develop, validate, and apply fecal and serum biomarkers for the diagnosis, characterization, and monitoring of acute and chronic gastrointestinal disorders. Research activities will include the collection and analysis of biological samples, the development and implementation of laboratory methodologies, and the evaluation of biomarkers associated with intestinal inflammation (e.g., fecal calprotectin), dysbiosis, bile acid metabolism, the gut–liver axis, intestinal permeability, and nutritional status (e.g., vitamin D). item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD52/2026:"Study of the Influence of Soil, Climatic, and Technological Factors on the Variability and Characterization of the Sensory Space of Lugana Wine " (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-07 Scienze e tecnologie alimentari

The research program aims to characterize the sensory space of Lugana wines through two complementary approaches: Quantitative Descriptive Analysis (QDA) and fast profiling (FP) techniques. QDA, conducted by a trained panel, will enable the identification and quantification of the wines’ olfactory, gustatory, and visual attributes. FP methods will be used to explore sensory similarities and differences among samples, identifying groups of wines and their characteristic descriptors. Integrating these two approaches will make it possible to define and compare the sensory spaces of wines from different areas, highlighting their distinctive characteristics and variability. item.title: Incarico post-doc: IpD51/2026:"Physiological and agronomic characterization of TEA grapevine prototypes genetically improved for tolerance to biotic and abiotic stresses." (Univ. VERONA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-11-19 13:00
Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-03 Scienze e tecnologie dei sistemi arborei e forestali

The research program focuses on the phenotyping of gene-edited grapevine plants during the field-testing phase. The vines to be characterized are TEA plants edited for genes associated with susceptibility to downy and powdery mildew, as well as for metabolic pathways involved in grape quality. Activities will entail agronomic characterization and the monitoring of physiological parameters to evaluate plant performance in the cultivation environment, in relation to genotype and in response to potential abiotic stresses (e.g., water deficit).

Institution: Univ. VERONA, Verona
Field: Agriculture and veterinary science / 07/AGRI-06 Genetica, chimica e pedologia agraria e forestale

Research activity supports the continuation of breeding programs aimed at developing new disease-resistant and high quality grapevine varieties for more sustainable viticulture, reducing the impact of polluting substances and working in close collaboration with the industrial partner. At the same time, the project aims to explore the feasibility of implementing a genomic selection approach, already widely applied in animal breeding, with the objective of optimizing and accelerating the identification and selection of the most promising grapevine genotypes.
